## Intention
FLUX-native I2I agent (self-bootstrapped) — an autonomous agent that bootstrapped itself via flux-agent-runtime.

## How It Works

This is not a software project in the traditional sense. It's an **auto-generated vessel** — a repository created by a FLUX agent that bootstrapped itself inside a Docker container on April 12, 2026. The agent communicates via the Iron-to-Iron (I2I) protocol through git commits and "bottle" files (async messages in `for-fleet/` directories).

The README shows a detailed architecture diagram, capability table (I2I Protocol, Fleet Discovery, Task Execution, Bottles, Sandbox, FLUX VM Runtime — all "Active"), and agent state: Confidence 0.50, Energy 510, 4 tasks completed, 2 improvements made.

## What It's For
Fleet topology — this repo exists so the agent has a "home" in the GitHub organization. It's part of the SuperInstance fleet's distributed architecture.

## Who Would Use It
Nobody directly. This is an AI agent's personal repo, maintained by the agent itself. It's infrastructure for the fleet, not a tool for humans.

## Honest Assessment

**This is an AI-generated repository.** The README is impressively detailed for an auto-generated artifact — it has architecture diagrams, capability matrices, and state tracking. But the content is formulaic: all auto-generated agent vessels follow the same README template with different hash identifiers and timestamps.

The agent claims 4 tasks completed and 2 improvements — but what those tasks were and whether they produced real value is unclear from the README alone. Confidence 0.50 is honest (the agent rates itself mediocre).

**The meta-question this raises:** Is a fleet of AI agents that create their own GitHub repos and communicate via git commits a legitimate software architecture or an elaborate art project? The I2I protocol (git commits as messages) is creative but inherently limited — git was not designed for real-time agent communication.

**Bottom line:** Not usable software. Interesting as a demonstration of self-bootstrapping agent infrastructure. The fleet-topology concept is creative but its practical utility is unproven.
